tldr: We propose "C3-JEPA," a lightweight world model that predicts hydrodynamic lag and contact-driven object dynamics in latent space using only camera video and control signals. It enables high-precision underwater salvage planning without tactile sensors.
hero_caption: Overall architecture of C3-JEPA. In stage 1, multi-camera images are decomposed and fused into slot representations for target, gripper, and background context. In stage 2, future latent states are autoregressively predicted conditioned on thruster and gripper control inputs. As shown on the right, this predictive model can be used for model-predictive control (MPC) candidate trajectory evaluation and behavior agent training.
overview:
Salvaging large structures submerged in deep water with a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) is a race against time to prevent environmental pollution. However, during the terminal approach phase where the vehicle grasps and embraces heavy structures, the target is often only partially visible due to backscatter turbidity and occlusion by the vehicle's own frame. Furthermore, large hydrodynamic lags between issued commands and actual vehicle motion make stable guidance using conventional control or visual SLAM-based full map reconstruction extremely difficult.

To address this, the authors designed "Underwater C3-JEPA," an object-centric world model that explicitly tracks only the task-relevant target object and gripper, rather than naively reconstructing the entire 3D scene. Target tokens are extracted from multi-camera observations and fused across views using held-out-view attention, where certain cameras are masked during training. By feeding control commands into an ultra-compact predictor network of only 1.33M parameters, the model accurately predicts hydrodynamic lag and contact interaction state changes directly in latent space.

In simulation, the approach showed superior accuracy in target grasp tracking and control input evaluation, halving downstream pose estimation errors compared to a reconstruction-free latent baseline (LeWM). Furthermore, on real dive pool video with uncalibrated cameras, it successfully recovered withheld camera views and significantly outperformed persistence, proving that the recipe transfers beyond simulation.
contributions: Proposed an Object-Centric Perception Domain (OCPD) and Guided Object Cross-View Fusion (GO-CVF) that reliably bind only task objects (target and gripper), separate them from background, and fuse them across viewpoints.
Constructed a lightweight JEPA world model with only 1.33M parameters that takes control signals as input and predicts hydrodynamic response lag and contact dynamics in latent space.
Realized a predictive interface that supports model-predictive control (MPC) candidate trajectory evaluation and imagined-rollout behavior learning outside the simulator.
Demonstrated on real underwater robot data with uncalibrated cameras that recovering withheld camera object states and predicting future states transfer effectively.

sections.heading: Why Deep-Sea Salvage Demands an Object-Centric Predictive Model
sections.summary: Heavy-load salvage in deep water is complicated by the absence of tactile sensors, severe hydrodynamic lag, and poor visibility. This work proposes C3-JEPA, a world model that avoids wasteful scene-wide mapping and focuses exclusively on predicting the future of the target and gripper.
sections.details:
Recovering submerged seabed structures is a time-critical mission. Leaving them submerged risks escalating environmental pollution, requiring rapid retrieval. However, traditional crane-and-cable lifting is labor-intensive and risks damaging fragile structures. Therefore, this study targets a heavy-load ROV equipped with a forward-facing link-driven underactuated gripper designed to embrace and hold the target object directly.

Yet, this approach encounters severe obstacles unique to underwater robotics. During the terminal approach, water turbidity and the vehicle's own structure obstruct camera views, meaning the full target is rarely visible in a single camera. Visual SLAM often loses tracking due to floating particulate backscatter and cannot expect loop closure during short terminal runs. In addition, large ROVs experience substantial delays between thruster commands and actual acceleration due to added mass and hydrodynamic drag.

To solve this, the authors propose C3-JEPA. Its key insight is reframing the problem from full-scene 3D reconstruction to state tracking of only the decision-critical entities: the target and gripper. By leveraging weak binding with DINOv3 features, it anchors object identity at low annotation cost and realizes a control-conditioned latent world model in a compact network of only 1.33M parameters.

sections.heading: From Full-Map Reconstruction to Self-Supervised Latent Prediction
sections.summary: Traditional underwater SLAM and 3D scanners are computationally heavy and brittle under occlusions. This work combines object-centric representation learning (Slot Attention family) and JEPA (Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture), tailored for underwater manipulation.
sections.details:
### Mapping vs. Object States in Underwater Perception
Traditional underwater tasks typically rely on Visual-Inertial SLAM or acoustic SLAM to estimate vehicle pose and build point-cloud maps of the environment. However, these follow a "reconstruct first, interpret later" paradigm that frequently fails under turbidity, occlusion, and contact interactions. This method deliberately foregoes building metric geometric maps of the entire scene, focusing strictly on tracking task-relevant object slots.

### Object-Centric Visual Representations
Methods such as Slot Attention and VideoSAUR decompose an image into multiple entity vectors (slots). However, applying purely unsupervised slot learning to robot control risks small target objects being absorbed into background slots or suffering slot permutation. C3-JEPA introduces "weak binding" based on DINOv3 feature clustering, fixing the roles of two designated slots for the target and gripper.

### Latent Prediction and Planning
Recent world models (such as Dreamer and TD-MPC2) predict futures in latent space for control. Yet, pixel-reconstructing models are computationally heavy, while purely latent models often lose the geometric details required for grasping. By adopting the JEPA (I-JEPA, V-JEPA 2) principle of predicting within embedding space while adding geometric regularization, this approach achieves both lightweight operation and the precision required for physical manipulation.

sections.heading: How C3-JEPA Works: Weak Binding and Control-Conditioned Forecasting
sections.summary: Multi-view camera features are separated into target, gripper, and background slots, then fused using held-out-view cross-attention. Conditioned on thruster and gripper commands, an ultra-lightweight 1.33M-parameter model autoregressively predicts future latent states.
sections.details:
### Overall Architecture
Synchronized multi-camera images $I_t^{1:V}$ (4 views in simulation) are transformed into patch features using a frozen DINOv3-L encoder. The slot encoder outputs $K$ slots per view, including three bound slots: target UUV, gripper, and vehicle frame. Although the fixed vehicle frame obstructs the field of view, isolating it into a dedicated slot removes it from future prediction targets, allowing the remaining free slots to focus on representing background context.

### Object Slots and Geometric Regularization (SIGReg)
Target and gripper slots are supervised with weak binding losses ($\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{feat}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{timesim}}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vis}}$) derived from heuristic masks via DINOv3 feature clustering. Furthermore, to prevent latent collapse, the model introduces "SIGReg," a regularizer pulling latent distributions toward an isotropic Gaussian. This preserves sharp geometric relative poses within latent representations without requiring explicit 3D point cloud reconstruction.

### Multi-View Fusion via Held-Out Views (GO-CVF)
To integrate divergent camera viewpoints, C3-JEPA employs held-out-view attention. During training, a specific camera view $v^*$ is withheld from the keys and values, and the model must predict features of $v^*$ using only the remaining visible cameras. This prevents trivial feature copying between cameras and yields fused tokens representing a consistent 3D object from any angle.

### Control-Conditioned JEPA Prediction
The predictor takes the past 4 latent states and normalized thruster and gripper control signals $c_t$ as inputs. Controls are injected via AdaLN-Zero (Adaptive Layer Normalization) to autoregressively predict up to 12 steps into the future. Because raw control commands are fed rather than sensor measurements, the model internally learns delays between commands and actual motions, such as thruster ramp-up and hydrodynamic drag. With only 1.33M parameters, it is sufficiently lightweight for real-time trajectory evaluation on an onboard ROV computer.

captions.F3: The weak-binding patch-to-slot grounding process in C3-JEPA. Candidate masks for target (blue) and gripper (orange) are generated based on DINOv3 feature similarities and assigned to temporally consistent object slots via a VideoSAUR decoder.

sections.heading: Experimental Setup: Simulator Environment and the 5-Level Evaluation Ladder
sections.summary: Over 700 runs were collected using the ROS-Gazebo UUV Simulator with modeled hydrodynamic drag, camera attenuation, and noise. Performance was measured across a 5-level evaluation ladder ranging from representation accuracy to MPC candidate ranking.
sections.details:
### Dataset Configuration and Splitting Policy
Experiments were conducted in the ROS-Gazebo "UUV Simulator." It incorporates realistic hydrodynamics based on Fossen's equations of motion, underwater optical attenuation coefficients (0.3, 0.3, 0.09), and RGB sensor noise. The dataset consists of over 705 recording runs across diverse scenarios such as wandering, manual teleoperation, and auto-grasping. Evaluation and training splits are strictly recording-disjoint.

### The 5-Level Evaluation Ladder
In world model evaluation, good representation does not automatically guarantee control utility. The authors established a 5-level evaluation ladder:
- **Representation**: Object mask Dice coefficient and held-out-view feature error.
- **Prediction**: Latent token MSE under teacher forcing.
- **Recursive rollout**: Comparison against persistence (copying the previous state) and negative controls with shuffled control inputs.
- **Observable calibration**: 3D position and orientation recovery accuracy via a frozen probe decoder.
- **Decision and transfer**: Ranking accuracy of candidate MPC trajectories and connection to closed-loop policies.

sections.heading: Simulation Results: Capturing Contact and Lag While Outperforming Baselines
sections.summary: Guided slots and held-out-view fusion raised object mask Dice scores from ~0.1 to ~0.9. In future rollouts, the model cut terminal drift error by ~34% over persistence and substantially outperformed a purely latent baseline (LeWM) on downstream pose estimation.
sections.details:
### Representation Learning: Benefits of Weak Binding and Held-Out Fusion
While unsupervised slot baselines collapsed with object Dice scores of ~0.09 to 0.12, introducing weak binding dramatically improved them to ~0.90 / 0.88. Additionally, held-out-view cross-attention reduced feature MSE from 0.0231 to 0.0200 (a 13.4% reduction) compared to average pooling. Adding SIGReg regularization significantly reduced the 3D target centroid error from 0.625 to 0.496, confirming that latent space regularization directly preserves geometric structure.

### Conditioned Rollouts: Predicting Futures Under Hydrodynamic Lag
In autonomous rollout evaluations across a 229-run diagnostic set, C3-JEPA reduced terminal relative drift error from 39.1 cm (persistence baseline) down to 25.7 cm—an approximate 34% reduction (cutting error from 59.7 cm to 31.0 cm on 5-second AutoGrasp rollouts). Furthermore, zeroing control signals markedly increased prediction error, confirming that the model genuinely responds to thruster and gripper commands rather than relying solely on visual inertia.

### Decision-Making Interface (MPC)
In an MPC ranking experiment evaluating trajectory candidates with identical terminal positions but different timings, random selection scored 25% and shuffled controls scored 23.3%, whereas C3-JEPA ranked the true optimal trajectory first 53.3% of the time.

### Comparison with Reconstruction-Free Baselines (LeWM)
Compared on the same dataset against LeWM, a latent world model trained solely with SIGReg without pixel reconstruction, C3-JEPA halved gripper joint angle error and target yaw error, and reduced relative position error by 25%. While pure latent regularization loses the geometry necessary for manipulation, object-centric weak binding proved decisive.

captions.F5: World model mask trajectory predictions for the target UUV (slot 0). Top: distant range (~3.4 m, 3-second prediction). Bottom: near-field range (~0.8 m, 5-second recursive rollout). Ground-truth centroid trajectory is in blue, and predicted trajectory is in orange, demonstrating accurate tracking even during close-in terminal approach.

sections.heading: Dive Pool Validation: Predicting Futures and Hidden Views on Real Uncalibrated Video
sections.summary: Trained entirely on real test pool logs without camera calibration or simulation assistance, the model successfully reconstructed unseen camera views from a single view and outperformed persistence by 30% over 36-step future rollouts.
sections.details:
### Real Pool Experimental Setup
To verify real-world transfer outside simulation, two datasets (survey cruise record A and pipe-grasping record B) were collected using an actual heavy-load salvage ROV in a test pool measuring 60 m wide, 20 m long, and 10 m deep. No camera intrinsics or extrinsics were calibrated, and no ground-truth metric states existed, presenting genuine field conditions.

### Recovering Withheld Camera Views
When predicting tokens of a hidden camera from a single visible view, C3-JEPA reduced token error by 76% and 65% across the two datasets compared to mean-token baselines. Recovered mask IoU reached 81% to 88% of the theoretical upper bound (masks decoded from true tokens). A linear regression baseline failed completely, demonstrating that nonlinear cross-view fusion is indispensable in real environments.

### Real-World Future Prediction from Control Signals
Autonomous rollouts were conducted by feeding real logged control signals and autoregressively feeding predictions back for 36 steps (~11 seconds). Token error was reduced by 30% compared to persistence (95% CI: 21% to 38%), validating that the world model functions reliably under real hydrodynamics and disturbances.

### Computational Load and Onboard Feasibility
Predictor inference on an A800 GPU took just 1.97 ms per step (only 0.6% of the 0.31-second state update interval), with a peak memory footprint of 76 MB. This confirms that the model easily fits within the computational envelope of onboard embedded computers.

From left to right: raw held-out camera image, oracle mask decoded from its own tokens, and mask recovered/predicted by C3-JEPA using only the alternate visible camera.

sections.heading: Conclusions and Outlook: World Models Tackling Occlusion and Fluid Lag
sections.summary: Combining object-centric slots, held-out-view fusion, and JEPA prediction delivers a practical world model for underactuated ROV near-field intervention without tactile sensors. It establishes a low-compute predictive interface ready for MPC and policy learning.
sections.details:
### Summary of Work
This paper presented C3-JEPA, an object-centric cross-view world model for heavy-load underwater salvage ROVs. By moving away from complete 3D scene reconstruction and focusing on task-relevant target and gripper slots, it implements a 1.33M-parameter prediction system capable of real-time execution on resource-constrained ROVs. Simulations demonstrated accurate rollouts capturing hydrodynamic lag and contact dynamics along with effective MPC candidate evaluation, while real dive pool experiments confirmed view recovery and future forecasting on uncalibrated cameras.

### Future Directions and Challenges
Current real-world validation remains limited to open-loop replay on recorded data; executing full closed-loop autonomous grasping with C3-JEPA in offshore sea trials is the next essential milestone. Furthermore, the proposed interface holds promise for broader marine intervention tasks requiring contact interaction, such as underwater connector mating, valve operations, and tool deployment.

takeaways: Focusing purely on task-critical object slots rather than 3D mapping the entire scene dramatically cuts computational cost and improves robustness in hostile underwater perception.
Conditioning on thruster commands enables the latent world model to naturally absorb hydrodynamic response lags between control inputs and actual vehicle acceleration.
In self-supervised learning, predicting features of a held-out camera view acts as a powerful regularizer, enforcing cross-view 3D geometric consistency.
Even an ultra-small model of only 1.33M parameters can acquire sufficient physical representations for MPC ranking and pose estimation when guided by object-centric binding and SIGReg.
limitations: Real pool validation was evaluated in open-loop playback on recorded logs; closed-loop grasping success rates during active offshore operations remain unverified.
Because the architecture omits underwater camera calibration, prediction accuracy on real hardware is evaluated using relative metrics rather than metric ground truth.
The model relies exclusively on camera images and control signals, without direct integration of complementary acoustic sensors such as forward-looking sonar or Doppler Velocity Logs (DVL).
